title: Interior Gaussian two-point inequality
statement: Let $a,b\in\mathbb R$ satisfy $a-b\in(0,1)$ and $a+b\in(0,1)$. For the Gaussian isoperimetric profile $U$, one has $U(a)\le\frac{\sqrt{U(a+b)^2+b^2}+\sqrt{U(a-b)^2+b^2}}{2}$.
replaced: Let $\Phi$ and $\varphi$ be the standard Gaussian distribution function and density, and put $Q=\Phi^{-1}$ and $I(p)=\varphi(Q(p))$ for $0<p<1$. If $a,b\in\mathbb R$ and $a-b,a+b\in(0,1)$, then $I(a)\le\bigl(\sqrt{I(a+b)^2+b^2}+\sqrt{I(a-b)^2+b^2}\bigr)/2$.
